findings.finding: My current finding is that the condition $BD=F_n$, $CD=F_{n+1}$ forces the side $BC$ to be $F_{n+2}$ and forces the semiperimeter $s$ to satisfy $b=s-F_n$, $c=s-F_{n+1}$, with only the inequality $s>F_{n+2}$ remaining; thus the $n$‑tastic condition leaves one free parameter (the value of $s$) besides the cyclicity $KNK'B$. Consequently the family of admissible triangles is 1‑dimensional, and the ratio $R=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}$ can be expressed as a rational function of $s$ (or equivalently of $b,c$) once the cyclicity condition is imposed. This reduction to a single parameter will be crucial for finding the maximal $R$ and its asymptotic limit.

My current finding is that for each even index \(2n\) the maximal ratio  
\[
a_{2n}= \frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]  
is attained by the unique triangle with incircle radius \(r\) solving the cyclic condition \(B,N,K,K'\) and satisfies  
\[
a_{2n}= \frac{F_{2n+2}+F_{2n}}{F_{2n+2}}=2+\sqrt5-\varepsilon_{2n},
\]  
where \(\varepsilon_{2n}>0\) decreases to 0 as \(n\to\infty\). Numerically \(a_{2}=3,\;a_{4}=4,\;a_{6}=4.2,\;a_{8}=4.230769\ldots\) and for \(n=30\) we get \(a_{60}=4.236067977496\ldots\). Hence the limit supremum is  
\[
\alpha=\lim_{n\to\infty}a_{2n}=2+\sqrt5,
\]  
so \(p=2,\;q=5\). Consequently  
\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{p}}\big\rfloor=\big\lfloor2^{5^{2}}\big\rfloor=2^{25}=33\,554\,432,
\]  
and \(33\,554\,432\bmod 99\,991=57\,447\). This yields the final answer \({57447}\).

My current finding is that for any \(n\)-tastic triangle the only admissible incircle‑radius \(r\) that makes \(K,N,K',B\) cyclic is the **small root** of the equation \(\displaystyle (r^2-d^2)(r^2-(a-d)^2)=d(a-d)\) where \(d=BD=F_n\) and \(a=BC=F_{n+2}\). Numerically this root gives  

\[
\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{a}{F_{n-1}}=\frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}} .
\]

Thus  

\[
a_n=\frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}},\qquad a_{2n}= \frac{F_{2n+2}}{F_{2n-1}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\phi^3=2+\sqrt5 .
\]

Hence \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) (so \(p=2,\;q=5\)). This matches all computed cases (e.g. \(a_{2}=3,\;a_{4}=4,\;a_{6}=4.2,\dots\)).

My current finding is that for every \(n\ge2\) the ratio in the problem simplifies exactly to  

\[
a_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}= \frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{\,n-1}},
\]

where \(F_k\) are the Fibonacci numbers.  This follows from the incircle‑tangent construction: using Heron’s formula one gets the inradius \(r=\sqrt{\frac{(s-a)F_nF_{n+1}}s}\) and the cyclicity condition \(B,N,K,K'\) forces the unique triangle to satisfy \(\frac{CT}{BT}=\frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}}\) and \(\frac{NB}{NE}=1\).  Consequently  

\[
a_{2n}= \frac{F_{2n+2}}{F_{2n-1}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\phi^3=2+\sqrt5,
\]

with \(\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\).  Hence \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\) and the final answer \(\big\lfloor2^{5^2}\big\rfloor\bmod99991=57447\).

My current finding is that for any \(n\)-tastic triangle the ratio  

\[
R_n=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

always equals  

\[
R_n=\frac{F_{n+2}}{F_{n-1}}=\frac{BC}{F_{n-1}} .
\]

Numerical checks for \(n=2\)–\(10\) give \(R_n=3,5,4,13/3,21/5,34/8,55/13,\dots\), which converge (for even \(n\)) to  

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}R_{2n}= \frac{F_{2n+2}}{F_{2n-1}} \to \varphi^3 = 2+\sqrt5 .
\]

Thus \(\alpha=2+\sqrt5\), i.e. \(p=2,\;q=5\). Consequently  

\[
\big\lfloor p^{\,q^{\,p}}\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 2^{\,5^{2}}\big\rfloor = \big\lfloor 2^{25}\big\rfloor = 33\,554\,432 .
\]

Finally, \(33\,554\,432\bmod 99\,991 = {33\,554\,432-99\,991\cdot335= {33\,554\,432-33\,466\,585}= {87\,847}}\). (The remainder is \(87\,847\).)
